direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale is very good, as it builds its world and New York City through the lens of queer culture and the clubbing scene, delivering some of the best-directed club sequences I've seen, which says a lot since I usually find clubbing scenes in movies tacky and poorly directed; the direction on a microscale has some moments that show his inexperience as a first-time feature director, but he still gets a good amount out of his actors, and the interpersonal scenes are where the comedy and the genuinely touching emotional moments come out, especially in the father-son relationship that makes this movie; the storytelling is very well done, using the clubbing scene to build the world while making the father-son relationship and how it affects the father's self-worth the main vehicle for the story; the tension is strong because you become so emotionally invested in this relationship and these characters that you're on edge whenever things go wrong

performance.comments: The fact that he wrote, directed, and starred in this movie is phenomenal; you can tell he's not the greatest actor, and it's really the filmmaking that makes the movie rather than his performance, but he's funny, carries the scenes he's in, and does a very good job in the emotional scenes, where he shows a good amount of depth; he also has really good chemistry with the child, to the point where you very much care about their relationship and what happens to them
Does a very good job as the emotional core of the movie and handles his scenes very well, and his great chemistry with the father is what really makes the movie
I genuinely thought she was the worst actress of the 2010s, and yet somehow she's actually fine, even pretty good, and plays her role well, which is the most shocking part of this whole movie

cast.comments: Made up of a lot of non-actors or very inexperienced actors who do fine, but they also bring out the comedy and the culture of the movie, have good chemistry, and play off each other very well to help the overall story

story.comments: The concept is so interesting, because while a father suddenly building a relationship with his son isn't the most original idea, setting it against the backdrop of New York's queer clubbing scene makes it feel fresh; the plot structure is pretty linear, using time jumps to separate the different parts of the story, from the exposition into the rising action and conflict, then into the climax and resolution; character writing is very strong, as you really care about Peter, a degenerate drug addict, drug dealer, and notorious partier in his thirties who can't hold down a relationship, and you see how much he grows by becoming a father and wanting to be a better person for his son, especially by the end, while his son slowly opening up to him makes the father-son relationship one you genuinely care about

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is very Gen Z-coded and queer-coded, and while some of it isn't the best writing and the profound moments aren't the most eloquent, the sentiments are there, making the movie entertaining, funny, and emotional through how the characters deliver their lines; the humor is very strong, with some of the funniest bits I've heard all year and so many jokes that hit, so even if it isn't technically a comedy, it feels like one; the symbolism centers on the father-son relationship, as a lost degenerate with zero self-esteem who uses drugs and partying to cope grows into a better person because of his son, all leading to an ending that's a little overt but the right call and really tugs at your emotions; the foreshadowing is good, planting roots that pay off in the conflict and climax

score.comments: Good, complementing the tone of the movie very well

soundtrack.comments: Full of the house music you'd actually hear in the club, incorporated well to emphasize the club sequences, and I very much enjoyed it

cinematography.comments: Shot very well on 35mm film, with a lot of grain that helps show New York and build the world, and while the interpersonal moments are shot in a pretty standard way, the clubbing sequences, with their lights and flashes, feel like a realistic and authentic club experience, and the use of focus to emphasize important moments, especially in the climax, is great

editing.comments: Sharp and polished, yet rough where it needs to be, making the clubbing sequences energetic and lively, and it's all well put together

sound.comments: The bumping bass in the club sequences makes the club experience feel authentic and lively, and the sound is good in those moments

production_design.comments: Set in New York, with well-designed club sets that help transport you to the New York clubbing and queer scenes

review.pacing: Paced perfectly, with just the right amount of content, so there's no need to add or cut anything
review.climax: The emotional peak of the movie, executed and shot very well, as it makes you tear up while showing the journey we went on with these characters, and it's exactly the right ending, so I applaud them for going that route
review.tone: A Gen Z queer clubbing comedy-drama that's both an emotional father-son drama and a genuinely funny comedy
review.final_notes: Saw a screening at Austin Film Festival
review.overall: Overall, 'Club Kid' is a well-made film that's one of the funniest yet most profound movies I've seen all year; it uses the NYC clubbing world as the backdrop for a father-son duo so emotional that it makes you want to laugh, cry, and cheer, which is all you can ask for in a good movie; Jordan Firstman hit it out of the park with this one, so I very much recommend it and really look forward to what he does next as both an actor and a filmmaker
